name: time_scaling
description: Does the DeepSets agent's advantage grow, shrink or hold as the per-turn time budget moves? DeepSetsBotExp vs SakkirinaScaled at per-turn budgets of 2, 5, 10, 20 and (optionally) 30 seconds, with the SAME scale applied to BOTH sides at every budget, 400 games each.
_which_agent: This config measures the blend agent, not the network-only one. SOT_ALPHA0 is written out as 0.7 in every row; that is DeepSetsBotExp's default (ALPHA_START), so it changes nothing and the completed run's results stand, but the config now states which agent it measures. At alpha0=0.7 DeepSetsBotExp is DeepSetsBlendBot, the 1st-place submission; at alpha0=0 it is DeepSetsBot. time_scaling's 10s row is therefore the same agent configuration as alpha_sweep's alpha0_0.7 row (--timeout 12 here, 10 there), while both equal_effort configs run alpha0=0, a different agent. A time-scaling row and an equal-effort row are not the same agent under two conditions.
_budget_note: Both agents derive their per-turn budget the same way: TurnTimeout = 9.8s * scale and per-move cap = 0.65s * scale. scale = budget/10 thus gives a self-imposed cap of 0.98*budget, the same 2% margin under the engine clock that the submitted agents use at the stock 10s. SOT_TIME_SCALE drives DeepSetsBotExp and SOT_BASELINE_TIME_SCALE drives SakkirinaScaled; every row sets both to the same number.
_timeout_note: Engine --timeout is budget + 2s. The engine clock is a per-turn budget accumulated across moves, so a turn that spends its whole allowance would land on the boundary and score TURN_TIMEOUT, making the tightest budgets look like the weakest agents. The aggregator reports timeouts separately for this reason: if they are not near zero, the margin is too small and the row's win rate is not usable. The 10s row is therefore not directly comparable to legacy_paper_benchmark.json, which used --timeout 10 with no margin.

matchups.label: budget_02s
matchups.note: Bot-side cap 1.96s/turn. The shallowest search in the config -- watch the disqualification column, since a shallower tree makes the no-isomorphic-match fallback fire more often.

matchups.label: budget_10s
matchups.note: Stock timing on both sides: bot-side cap 9.8s, exactly what the submitted agents and stock SakkirinaSolo use. The reference row.

matchups.label: budget_30s
matchups.note: OPTIONAL, and the most expensive row by far -- roughly 3x the wall clock of the 10s row for the same 400 games. Skip it by simply not submitting its task-id range (--dry-run prints the range); it is last in the config so leaving it out changes no other row's task ids.
